text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- Fritz Verzetnitsch, head of both the Austrian and European trade union congress, calls for a new Maastricht treaty which includes a seven percent unemployment threshold for countries wanting to join EMU. Heavy fines should apply to those missing the criterium, he said.

- Civil servants in the finance ministry have gone on a 24-hour strike to protest against changes in their pension schemes and other austerity measures imposed by the government. The reform of the public sector's pension system is supposed to result in 2.5 billion schillings in savings.
- The Austrian embassy in Greece was hit by fire bombs during a demonstration against the European Union.
- Austria's trade balance with Switzerland turned to a deficit of 1.7 billion schillings on the back of increased capital exports to the neighbouring country in 1996.
- German and Austrian Finance Ministers, Guenter Rexrodt and Hannes Farnleitner, said at a meeting they were against a job creation initiative by the European Commission.
- Austria's civl servants' union threatens the entire public sector may go on strike against the government's austerity drive.
- Builder Era Bau will be completely restructured and will focus more on its international business.
- The Austrian Business Agency has brought some 740 million schillings in new investments to Austria, creating 600 jobs in the five months to May alone.
- Chancellor Viktor Klima says the first members of Europe's planned single currency may be chosen before the spring of 1998.
- State secretary of finance Wolfgang Ruttensdorfer says planned spending cuts in the public sector are fair and balanced.
- Austria's tourism balance is still slightly positive, but the country's overall trade balance is deeply in the red.

- Die Erste savings bank and GiroCredit are expected to merge in September. An eight billion schillings capital increase is expected to result from the sale of new shares via the bourse and by taking on new strategic partners towards the end of the year.
- Austria is becoming increasingly dependent on imported natural gas.
